authoredSolutions.1: Pressure has dimensions \(\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}\), so \(Pt\) carries \(\mathrm{N\,s\,m^{-2}}\). For viscosity, Stokes' relation \(F = 6\pi\eta r v\) gives \[\eta = \frac{F}{6\pi r v} \sim \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}} = \mathrm{N\,s\,m^{-2}}.\] So \(Pt\) and \(\eta\) share the same dimensions and Assertion A is true. Reason R states \(\eta = \dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Velocity gradient}}\), which omits the area factor; the correct definition is \(\eta = \dfrac{F}{A\,(dv/dx)}\). Hence R is false. The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.2: With \(a = k^{2}rt^{2}\) and \(a = v^{2}/r\), \[\frac{v^{2}}{r} = k^{2}rt^{2} \Rightarrow v = krt.\] The tangential acceleration is \(a_{t} = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = kr\), so the tangential force is \(F_{t} = mkr\). Only the tangential component does work, so \[P = F_{t}v = (mkr)(krt) = mk^{2}r^{2}t.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.3: Since \(\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\omega t\right)=\cos\omega t\), the equations are \(x = 4\cos\omega t\) and \(y = 4\sin\omega t\). authoredSolutions.4: Apply the parallel-axis theorem for the tangents and the perpendicular-axis theorem for the diameters. Solid sphere about a tangent: \(I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2}+MR^{2} = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^{2}\), so A matches II. Hollow sphere about a tangent: \(I = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^{2}+MR^{2} = \dfrac{5}{3}MR^{2}\), so B matches I. Ring about a diameter: \(2I_{d} = MR^{2}\Rightarrow I_{d} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}\), so C matches IV. Disc about a diameter: \(2I_{d} = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}\Rightarrow I_{d} = \dfrac{1}{4}MR^{2}\), so D matches III. The required pairing is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III, which is the first option. The correct choice is A.

authoredSolutions.6: The drop has diameter \(2\ \mathrm{cm}\), so \(r = 1\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.01\ \mathrm{m}\). Hence \[\Delta E = T\,\Delta A = 0.075\times 12\pi r^{2} = 0.075\times 12\pi (0.01)^{2} \approx 2.8\times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.7: For an adiabatic change of \(\mu\) moles, \(Q=0\), so the first law gives \(W = -\Delta U = -\mu C_{V}\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right)\). Using \(C_{V} = \dfrac{R}{\gamma-1}\), \[W = -\frac{\mu R\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right)}{\gamma-1} = \frac{\mu R\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right)}{1-\gamma},\] so Statement I is true. Since \(Q=0\), \(\Delta U = -W\); if work is done on the gas then \(W<0\), so \(\Delta U>0\) and the temperature rises. Statement II is also true. The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.8: Statement I says the field near a point may increase when a positive charge is brought there. The charge's own field adds to the existing field on one side and subtracts on the other, so at points where the two are parallel the resultant does increase; the qualifier 'may' makes the statement true. Statement II is the standard result that a dipole in a non-uniform field experiences a net force, since \[F_{\text{net}} = qE(x+d)-qE(x) \approx p\frac{dE}{dx} \neq 0\] whenever the field gradient is non-zero along the dipole axis. Both statements are true, so the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.9: Charges \(q/2\) at A and \(q/2\) at C are each a distance \(a\) from D, and \(q\) at B is a distance \(a\sqrt{2}\) from D. The charge at B contributes \(\dfrac{kq}{2a^{2}}\) along the same line, so \[E_{D} = \frac{kq}{a^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_{0}a^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\right).\] The correct choice is A.

authoredSolutions.16: The two input diodes feed node X, which is pulled up to \(10\ \mathrm{V}\) through R and drives the base of the npn transistor. If either A or B is low, that diode conducts and clamps X low, the transistor is cut off and the collector Y sits at the supply, i.e. \(Y=1\). Only when both A and B are high do both diodes stop conducting, X rises, the transistor saturates and pulls Y to ground, i.e. \(Y=0\). The output is therefore low only for \(A=B=1\), which is the NAND function \[Y = \overline{AB}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.17: A junction diode has two terminals. Under forward bias it conducts and shows a low resistance on the multimeter; under reverse bias it blocks and shows a very high resistance. Assertion A is true, Reason R is true, and R is precisely why A holds. The correct choice is A.
